$comment: 🎚️ What a dragged inline slider costs, as rows. A press is a run of `nodeGraphEdit` dispatches carrying ONE top-level `gesture` (the release adds `commit: true`, a host cancel `abort: <reason>` with no operations): the framework scrub machine (design §13.1) keeps every tick provisional, so the committed document moves only at the release, and the whole press lands as ONE edit stamped with ONE tool transaction whose op is the ABSOLUTE `change-slider-value` leaf. `committed` is the committed slider value after each dispatch (null = the base value). Language-agnostic: the Rust law is `✏️editor/🎮️commands/✏️node-graph-edit/🧪️tests/🔬️unit`, the host half's twin is `📺️renderer/🧑‍🎨engine/🧪️tests/🎚️continuous-gesture-lane`.

presses.why: a 1 s drag produced 29 history entries and 24 evaluations before the press became a tool transaction
keying on the widget alone would swallow every later press of that slider into one undo step
a press the host cancels (blur, lost capture, unmount) must leave neither an edit nor a moved value
an agent or palette value with no press identity is one plain edit labelled by its leaf
an unchanged value yields no leaf, so the release commits an empty transaction: no edit

uiScope.$comment: 🐢️ What ONE slider tick invalidates. Everything absent here was re-rendered on every frame of a drag before this rule.

liveEvaluations.$comment: 🎚️ The host lane's ceiling, asserted by the TypeScript twin over the same numbers: one round trip in flight and one owed value, however fast the user drags.
